coordination_failures: Extremely low resource grant rate (20 out of 124 requests) suggests poor inter-agency coordination or allocation protocols.
Repeated exhaustion of ambulances (27 times) and repair crews (17 times) points to inadequate resource forecasting.
High rejection of 'repair_road' requests (9 times) likely delayed infrastructure recovery in multiple zones.
headline: Effective Mission Completion with Critical Resource Shortages

key_moments.description: Resolved two severity-4 missions (m3, m4), saving 40 lives with minimal losses.
Completed three mid-phase missions (m6, m7, m8); harbor infrastructure repair resulted in net loss of life.
Simultaneously resolved medical surge and infra repair in residential north, saving 28 but losing 8.
Final mission (m9) resolved late with high loss ratio (4 saved, 8 lost), indicating resource strain.

lessons: Pre-position critical resources based on early mission severity to avoid pool exhaustion.
Establish priority protocols for resource grants to reduce rejection of essential requests.
Monitor loss-to-save ratios per mission type to reallocate crews dynamically.
Improve road repair coordination—delays cascade into rescue and medical response times.
Maintain reserve ambulance capacity during surge events to prevent preventable fatalities.
what_worked: All 11 missions were resolved with zero failures, demonstrating strong operational follow-through.
Early high-severity missions (m2, m3, m4) were addressed within 6 ticks, limiting initial casualties.
Panic remained at 0.0 throughout, indicating effective public communication and perceived control.
